name: 石を５分見せられたら、あなたの「悪役スイッチ」は入る？(更新版・最新仕様)

p_3eb9a8bf3f.sentence: Another test found stone viewers likelier to cut rewards, regardless of tendency.
p_3eb9a8bf3f.prev: Stone viewers enjoying others’ pain cut rewards more often than magician viewers.

p_2d1f77d03c.sentence: If You Had to Watch a Stone for Five Minutes, Would Your “Bad-Guy Switch” Turn On?

p_ee502cde40.sentence: This goes on for five minutes.
p_ee502cde40.next: But you, the viewer, can still do one thing: make someone else’s reward smaller.

p_23ba3d1ee9.sentence: But it comes from an online experiment with people in the United States.
p_23ba3d1ee9.next: They were put into groups at random.

p_8f6445211a.sentence: They could change it by 10 cents each time, up to 50 cents in all.
p_8f6445211a.prev: They could make another person’s reward smaller, make it bigger, or do nothing.
p_8f6445211a.next: The stone on the screen stayed quiet, while the viewers were given “a little power.”

p_1b59e078e9.sentence: You may want to say, “So, it really depends on personality.”
p_1b59e078e9.prev: For people who felt this less strongly, there was no clear difference.
p_1b59e078e9.next: But there is more to the story.

p_623dbba84f.sentence: If we look only at personality, we may miss something.
p_623dbba84f.prev: People who watched the stone video were more likely to make another person’s reward smaller than people in the other groups.
p_623dbba84f.next: We need to ask not only what kind of person someone is, but also what they can do in that situation.

p_f67b19ede3.sentence: But it is too soon to say, “Add a button to make rewards bigger and bring world peace!”
p_f67b19ede3.prev: Now we also notice how the stage is set.

p_c9d3934b22.sentence: Even so, we see boring moments a little differently now.
p_c9d3934b22.prev: We cannot use its results directly to explain everyday meanness or boredom that lasts a long time.
p_c9d3934b22.next: We can ask not only, “What mustn’t I do?”

p_b1fb260f49.sentence: They were put into groups at random.
p_b1fb260f49.prev: But it comes from an online experiment with people in the United States.
p_b1fb260f49.next: One group watched a five-minute video of a stone, where nothing happened.

p_6501a5a67e.sentence: We do not know if giving people a choice to make rewards bigger can stop meanness.
p_6501a5a67e.prev: We cannot say the choices alone caused the different results.
p_6501a5a67e.next: The experiment looked only at brief boredom.

p_43505540e7.sentence: So, did boredom become fuel for being mean?
p_43505540e7.prev: The stone on the screen stayed quiet, while the viewers were given “a little power.”
p_43505540e7.next: People who strongly liked seeing others suffer were more likely to make the other person’s reward smaller after watching the stone video than after watching the magician video.

p_5d45a009b0.sentence: We thought we were reading a profile of the person.
p_5d45a009b0.prev: We need to ask not only what kind of person someone is, but also what they can do in that situation.
p_5d45a009b0.next: Now we also notice how the stage is set.
